events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.45)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI and metered, so extra distance does feed the fare: the excess-distance line alone is $3.06 (2.17 km × $1.4104/km, the trip's distance fare ÷ distance km) [F4][F7][RD-2]. One off-route segment is established by the trace: 14:28–14:34, +1.94 km off the optimal route [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it: there is no traffic incident on the replaced stretch, and the Ayer Rajah Expressway speed-band-2 record (14:10–14:28) can at most corroborate, not exempt on its own [F12][F15][RD-4].

RD-5 is the live question and it is not settled. The driver proposed the route change ("can I go round via Clementi Road?") and the rider answered "Sure, no problem."; the chat is complete and both messages are timestamped [F8][F9][F10]. Timing favours the rider's own account of a prior agreement — the agreement came at 14:31, before the segment's 14:28:45 cut-off is not satisfied (the message is at 14:31, i.e. after the segment start), so consent for the segment as measured is not established by timestamp, and the driver's post-trip statement that the rider said sure is not independent consent [F11][F8][F9][RD-5]. The agreement is SPECIFIC (a named road, Clementi Road), so under RD-5 it covers driving on Clementi Road only, and the record must tie the segment to that road. Nothing in the fact table ties the driven path to Clementi Road, and nothing places it elsewhere [F3][F8][G13]. That is exactly the scope-unreadable case: the finding is undetermined, not exempt and not automatically counts, per the trace's RD-5 rule [RD-5].

Because that undetermined finding changes the amount (it decides whether 1.94 km × $1.4104/km ≈ $2.74 is refunded, or $0), the case must go to a person [G12][G13][RD-5]. (For reference, if the segment counted the amount would be 1.94 × $1.4104 = $2.7362 ≈ $2.74.) No RD-3 stop exists in this segment, and no rider-named stop was requested [F3][RD-3]. The waiting line billed ($0.11) is a metered wait unit under RD-3(c) and stays [F5][RD-3]. RD-6 does not trigger: the driver has no previous upheld route dispute (route: 0) [F18][RD-6].

(3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts.
